text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
-Norway will most probably sign a long-term agreement for delivering natural gas to Denmark. The contract is worth 25 billion crowns and will run for a period of 25 years.

-Sponsors and other VIP guests will not be served alcohol at the world cup in downhill skiing at Kvitfjell near Lillehammer this weekend. Local politicians refused to allow alcohol at the event on grounds that sports and alcohol do not mix.

-Norway's Aker RGI has entered negotiations to sell its 50 percent-owned clothing company Helly Hansen for 400 millioner crowns. Aker RGI refused to say who the byer is and would not comment on weather it is a Norwegian or foreign company.
-Despite higher turnovers, profits in Norwegian listed companies are falling. Experts warn against an overheated market.
-Christian Ringnes, who leads one of Norway's largest real estate companies, says he expects demand for real estate to remain high throughout the year.
-Industrial giant Norsk Hydro presented disappointing 1996 profits, sending the share in a free fall on the Oslo Bourse.
